prompt: Stage 3-3, level 6, 55 HP, 46 gold, three losses in a row. Earlier, at 2-3 with 88 HP and no pairs, you let the losses run and banked the streak gold; it worked. Now the board has one 2-star and no items on the carry, and stage-3 losses are costing you 8 to 10 HP each. Same play again?

options.label: No. Slam the AD item on the carry, buy the carry copy for the 2-star, and roll below 50 for front-line upgrades: three more losses at stage-3 damage leave you near 25 entering stage 4
Yes: streak gold plus interest is the same maths at every stage; keep losing to 4-1 and roll then with 70 gold
Yes, but only until 3-5, then level to 7 and roll

explanation:
A loss streak is affordable when the HP it costs is cheap, and HP is cheap in stage 2: a 2-3 loss against a four-unit board costs 3 to 6 HP, so at 88 HP you could lose the whole stage and enter stage 3 above 65 with a fat bank. Stage 3 is a different price: six-unit boards and stage damage make each loss 8 to 10, and stage-4 losses are 12 and more. From 55 HP, three more losses put you around 28 at 4-1, where one bad rolldown is an 8th. The bank you would gain (about 10 extra gold over three rounds) does not buy back 30 HP.

So the play flips: spend now. The AD item on the carry, the copy that makes him 2-star, then roll under 50 for the front-line upgrades until the fights are close. Sitting at 50 with a board that loses every round is the mistake the whole lesson exists for. 'Until 3-5' is the same mistake with a date on it: two more losses at 9 HP each is 37 at the point you finally act.
principle: A loss streak is a stage-2 tool. From stage 3 on, count the HP per loss before you agree to another one.
commonMistake: Copying the stage-2 loss streak into stage 3 because it 'worked last time', without noticing each loss now costs twice the HP.
hint: Multiply the HP per loss at this stage by the losses left until you would act, and see where that leaves you at 4-1.
